question: Is the frozen released input corpus complete, and does the shipped pipeline run on it unchanged?

build.method: git archive of the pushed commit, extracted to node-local scratch, cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release inside the apptainer container
build.note: the same edge source and recipe as ticket 288's from-commit build; the binary md5 is compared against a28d10afab2b50bbe750d599ee2b7214 (ticket 287/288/289 binary)

manifests: MANIFEST_released.tsv (143 rows: pot, piece, points, bytes, md5, header_ok)
MANIFEST_derived.tsv (5 rows: piece, source_mesh, mesh_md5, points, pcd_md5, bytes)
input.no_sampling: no CloudCompare run: the cloud is taken as released, so this run's lanes are not a new draw

steps: inv290.py: every released md5/points/bytes and every derived md5/points/bytes/source-mesh md5 against the manifests; coverage of the 148-piece scored corpus against ticket 284's phase0-table.tsv; ascii vs binary and FIELDS per class
build both binaries from the commit
probe: Dataset/Point as a directory symlink to the whole corpus, POT_NAME=Pot_A, 25 s bounded, to see whether the stage reads through a symlink (and therefore would process all 148)
real run: Dataset/Point/Pot_J/<piece>_Point.pcd as a FILE-level symlink into the corpus; mesh stage with SFS_AXIS_FILE set; edge stage on the shipped defaults
determinism: the same Temp/Data inputs and the same edge binary again in a clean tree, exports compared by md5

score290.py: both lanes against the authors' reference with the project scorer, ticket 289's exports re-scored on the same basis, nearest-neighbour spread between the two runs' lines, lengths, and the overlay picture
geometry deleted: exports, kept faces, staging trees, node-local build tree; out/GEOMETRY_DELETED.txt written
parameters: shipped defaults only; no SFS_* switch set except SFS_AXIS_FILE (required by ticket 277); no threshold, default or code change
bar: median <= 2.0 mm and coverage(ours -> authors) >= 90 against the authors' breaklines
authors_rule: Pot J Piece 09's reference lines are ruled wrong (ticket 289), so the lane rows are a drop-in comparison against ticket 289, not a bar tally
